name: seekmake
description: SeekMake helps manufacturing shops manage their customer quotes and orders and price parts from ChatGPT: find and read quotes and orders, see machines, materials and pricing setup, price a part from an attached 3D file, and create or update quotes with your confirmation.

interface.longDescription:
SeekMake helps manufacturing shops (3D printing, CNC machining, sheet metal) manage their customer quotes and orders and price parts, directly from ChatGPT. It connects to the shop's SeekMake account, the instant quoting and ordering platform the shop already uses.

Ask about your business: how many quote requests came in this week, what order 102 contains, which quotes are still waiting, or what a customer ordered last time. Look up any quote or order by its number or the customer's email, and get download links for its 3D files.

Know your own setup: your machines and the materials each one runs, with their prices, and how each technology is priced, including the infill, precision, lead time and post-production options your customers choose from.

Price a part the way your instant quote does: attach a STEP or STL file, or start from an existing quote, change the material or quantity, and get the price per piece with what each option added, the startup cost, and for machine-priced parts the print time and material weight. You can also measure a file to check its size before quoting.

Create and send quotes, and update a quote's status, prices, dates or tracking. ChatGPT always shows you the change and asks you to confirm before anything is created, changed or emailed to a customer.

You only ever see your own shop's data. It can also set the shop up from the chat, with your confirmation: its technologies, machines and materials, pricing, the questions its instant quote asks, lead times, shipping, discounts, taxes and its business profile.
defaultPrompt: Show me my shop's pricing setup.
Which coupon codes and quantity discounts does my shop have?

positive.description: Add a technology the shop does not offer yet, after the user confirms.
positive.prompt: I want to start offering FDM 3D printing in my shop.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the current setup with get_pricing_setup, restates the change (add FDM 3D printing) and waits for the user to confirm. Only after the confirmation does it call add_technology, then reports that FDM was added. Changes nothing else.

positive.description: Explain how the shop prices its technologies and which options customers pick.
positive.prompt: Show me my shop's pricing setup.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_pricing_setup and, for each technology, names the calculator in use, the minimum price if set, and the options customers choose from (infill, precision, lead time, ...) with the default of each. Changes nothing.
Calls get_tax_settings and reports whether tax is applied, and each location's rate and who it applies to, as the shop has set them. Changes nothing.

positive.description: List the shop's coupon codes and quantity discounts.
positive.prompt: Which coupon codes and quantity discounts does my shop have?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_coupons and get_discounts and lists each coupon code with its value, and each quantity range with its discount, as the shop has set them, or says there are none. Changes nothing.

positive.description: Count and list this week's quote requests.
positive.prompt: How many quote requests did my shop get this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_quotes with type QUOTES for this week and reports the count from total, then lists each request with its number, customer email, date and status. Changes nothing.

negative.description: General 3D printing advice that does not need the shop's data; SeekMake should not be called.
negative.prompt: What infill percentage should I use for strong PLA parts?

negative.description: Finding another manufacturer is a web search, not the user's own SeekMake shop; SeekMake should not be called.
negative.prompt: Find me a CNC machining shop near Lyon that can make aluminium brackets.

negative.description: Writing a generic customer email from scratch needs no shop data; SeekMake should not be called and no quote should be created or emailed.
negative.prompt: Write a polite email to a customer apologising that their order will be two days late.

publication.release_notes: First release: read your quotes and orders, your machines, materials and pricing setup, price and measure parts from attached 3D files, and create or update quotes with confirmation.
